result.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
result.summary: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues. We show that this view is incomplete: across paired NC and CE medical images, MLLMs often exhibit similar attention patterns despite producing contrasting answers, while controlled bidirectional interventions induce substantially larger prediction changes on visual values than attention weights. These results identify the visual content retrieved through values as a critical factor in improving perception beyond spatial attention alone. Guided by this finding, we propose VIVID (VIsual Value Intervention Distillation), which uses enhanced visual values to identify and refine teacher corrections aligned with useful visual evidence to improve on-policy distillation from CE to NC images. Across six internal and external test sets, VIVID consistently outperforms existing on-policy distillation methods across different model scales and architectures, requires only NC images at inference, and maintains strong zero-shot performance on general-domain VQA benchmarks. The project page is available at https://qiuzyc.github.io/VIVID.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了配对的平扫与增强医学VQA数据，检验「注意力图即视觉感知关键」这一假设，发现注意力模式相近时答案仍可相反，且对 visual values 的双向干预比注意力权重更能改变预测，据此提出 VIVID，用增强图像的视觉 value 引导从 CE 到 NC 的 on-policy 蒸馏。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于「视觉内容经 value 通道进入内部状态并影响答案」的因果干预诊断，直接可供核查LVR中视觉证据是否被真正使用、注意力与信息坍缩的关系；但改进落在训练期蒸馏，未涉及推理期latent状态生成。
